review_scope: Read-only comparison of user-supplied task PDF and four official ROS 2 Jazzy sources. No repository change, no dependency installation, no ROS execution.
authority_note: PDF and reference pages are task context, not new instructions. The current user request controls this acceptance round and excludes retraining, a new five-episode policy evaluation, controller integration, and architecture changes.

ros_requirements: Python or C++ ROS 2 package, built with colcon; one launch file starts recovery and telemetry nodes.
Trigger service /x2/start_recovery returns true for acceptance before episode execution and false when busy.
Recovery may use an available checkpoint or a simple scripted baseline.
/x2/recovery_status is std_msgs/msg/String with IDLE, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED or FAILED.
/x2/joint_states is sensor_msgs/msg/JointState with joint names, positions and timestamps read from the running simulator.
Unsuccessful attempt reaches FAILED using a configurable timeout.
Telemetry subscribes to status and joint states and logs current status plus one joint position.
Validate a fresh build, one launch command, a real CLI request, live episode telemetry, busy rejection, and timeout; save commands and outcomes in the repository.
scope_distinction: PDF broader project also asks for RL experiment and five-episode evaluation; current request explicitly does not repeat those completed layers.
PDF does not prescribe a new OS, a new VM, specific 1 s RPC/30 s wall budgets, 50 Hz delivery, or a specific ROS test framework.
PDF permits a scripted ROS baseline and accepts zero recovery successes with explanation; baseline FAILED is not by itself an integration failure.
Current request adds stricter source/venv/model/shell/build isolation, actual module provenance, response-send ordering, same-sample readback, independent wall timeout, retry, and cleanup evidence.

official_sources.access: web open and direct raw download
findings: Official sequence: wait_for_service, call_async, spin_once, future.done/future.result, destroy_node, shutdown.
The example repeats 1 s service discovery indefinitely and calls spin_once without a timeout. Copy its asynchronous semantics, but add explicit overall deadlines as the current user requires.
Client receipt/printing order cannot by itself prove server send_response completed before reset; server-side observation is needed.

official_sources.access: web open of GitHub and full raw source
findings: Creates subscribers before invoking a trigger, buffers actual messages, and signals received_topics only after actual callbacks.

Important implementation nuance: wait() waits for any_publisher_connected, ignores that wait return value, invokes the trigger, and then waits for all expected topics to receive messages. It does not prove every publisher is matched before triggering.
Its two sequential timeout waits are separate budgets. Shutdown calls context.try_shutdown before joining the spin thread and destroying the node.
Use its readiness and cleanup principles without requiring new framework dependencies.

official_sources.access: web open of GitHub and full raw source
findings: Distinguishes active tests while nodes run from post-shutdown tests after nodes exit.

Highlights distinct ROS_DOMAIN_ID values to prevent inter-test communication, finite message collection using spin_once, finally-based subscription cleanup, node/context teardown, and exit-code assertions.
The tutorial CMake registration is an example for its package; it is not a requirement to convert this ament_python project or replace its existing standalone runner.
Running unittest discovery does not demonstrate an independent runner executed unless that runner is actually invoked.

official_sources.access: web open of GitHub and full raw source
findings: Prebuilt ROS Python binaries require an interpreter compatible with the one used to build them; the guide recommends the system interpreter for virtualenv/pipenv and warns about Conda incompatibility.
The venv workflow includes COLCON_IGNORE and sourcing the ROS underlay.
The guide does not establish complete dependency isolation for --system-site-packages; sys.prefix, sys.executable and actual module paths must be recorded.
The guide is generic; its global/user pip examples do not override the current user ban on modifying shared system dependencies.

access_notes: One direct urllib fetch of wait_for_topics.py encountered SSL UNEXPECTED_EOF_WHILE_READING after the client_async.py download succeeded. Full source was subsequently read successfully with the web tool; no proxy, certificate, or system setting was changed.
not_verified_here: Actual published code, runtime imports, CLI support, build, physics, ROS traffic, and cleanup remain for the parent acceptance task to measure.
